=== BEGIN ARTIFACT TOPOLOGY.md ===
## Declarations

## story architecture
summary:      Stand up the Python project tree, environment, dependency manifest, and pytest runner.
type:         foundational
kind:         capability
phase:        1
implements:   ARCHITECTURE.md
stack:        common.md, python.md
provides:     project tree, pytest runner
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  Create the application root with pyproject.toml, a committed uv.lock, a .venv created by uv venv,
  a tests/ directory, and a conftest.py that exposes the cli_runner fixture.

  Python 3.11 or newer, standard library only at runtime. pytest is the only dev dependency.

  Never read sources/run.sh or the snapshot from application code.

## story cli-foundation
summary:      Publish the cli package, main entry point, cli_runner test helper, and the quakes launcher.
type:         foundational
kind:         capability
phase:        1
implements:   FEATURE-CliFoundation.md
stack:        python.md, cli.md
provides:     cli.main, cli.testing.cli_runner, ./quakes
depends:      architecture
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  Create cli/__init__.py with main(argv=None) -> int and cli/testing.py with cli_runner per the
  Foundation Contract in TECHNOLOGY_STACK.md.

  Create an executable file named quakes at the application root that calls cli.main and exits
  with its return value.

  Dispatch is a skeleton here; later stories register the commands.

## story options
summary:      Parse and validate the command, options, and file argument, with usage errors exiting 2.
type:         service
kind:         capability
phase:        2
implements:   FEATURE-Options.md
covers:       CLI-001
stack:        python.md, cli.md
provides:     parse_args
depends:      cli-foundation
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  Command first, options in any order, file last. Each command accepts only its listed options.
  Decimals match -?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?. --n is a positive integer. --lat in -90..90, --lon in
  -180..180, --radius positive, near requires all three. Missing or extra file, unknown command,
  and no command are usage errors.

  Do not use argparse default error behavior that prints to stdout; usage errors raise a UsageError
  that the dispatcher maps to exit 2.

## story exit-codes
summary:      Map usage and operational failures to exit codes 2 and 1 with silent stdout and one stderr line.
type:         service
kind:         capability
phase:        2
implements:   FEATURE-ExitCodes.md
covers:       CLI-002
accepts:      st-007
stack:        python.md, cli.md
provides:     UsageError, OperationalError, exit code mapping
depends:      options
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  Define UsageError (exit 2) and OperationalError (exit 1). main catches them, writes exactly one
  diagnostic line to stderr, and writes nothing to stdout. Reports build their full output before
  writing so a failure leaves stdout empty. Success, including empty reports, is exit 0.

## story formatting
summary:      Format times, magnitudes, depths, distances, and CSV output.
type:         service
kind:         capability
phase:        2
implements:   FEATURE-Formatting.md
covers:       FMT-001
stack:        python.md
provides:     format_time, format_mag, format_mean, format_decimal, write_csv
depends:      architecture
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  Time is UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ truncated to whole seconds from epoch milliseconds. Magnitude has
  one decimal. mean_mag has two decimals and depth_km and distance_km one decimal, all rounded half
  up using decimal.Decimal with ROUND_HALF_UP on the exact repr of the value. CSV is written with
  the csv module, lineterminator "\n", UTF-8 stdout.

## story feed-validation
summary:      Read a saved GeoJSON file and validate that it is a FeatureCollection.
type:         service
kind:         capability
phase:        2
implements:   FEATURE-FeedValidation.md
covers:       READ-001
stack:        python.md
provides:     read_feed
depends:      exit-codes
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  read_feed(path) returns the features list. An unreadable file, non-JSON content, or a value that
  is not an object with "type" equal to "FeatureCollection" and a list "features" raises
  OperationalError.

## story event-extraction
summary:      Extract event fields from features and exclude null-magnitude events.
type:         service
kind:         capability
phase:        2
implements:   FEATURE-EventExtraction.md
covers:       READ-002
stack:        python.md
provides:     extract_events, Event
depends:      feed-validation
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  Read id, properties.mag, properties.place, properties.time, properties.tsunami, and
  geometry.coordinates [lon, lat, depth_km]. Ignore every other field. A feature whose mag is null
  is dropped. A null place stays None here; regions handle it.

## story mag-filter
summary:      Apply the --min-mag filter to events.
type:         service
kind:         capability
phase:        2
implements:   FEATURE-MagFilter.md
covers:       READ-003
accepts:      st-005
stack:        python.md
provides:     filter_events
depends:      event-extraction
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  filter_events(events, min_mag) keeps events with mag >= min_mag; None keeps all.

## story summary
summary:      The summary report.
type:         service
kind:         capability
phase:        3
implements:   FEATURE-Summary.md
covers:       SUM-001
stack:        python.md, cli.md
provides:     quakes summary
consumes:     read_feed, extract_events, filter_events, write_csv, parse_args
depends:      mag-filter, formatting
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  Header events,first,last,min_mag,max_mag,mean_mag,tsunami. One row; first and last are the
  earliest and latest times; tsunami counts events equal to 1. No events yields 0,,,,,,0.

## story top
summary:      The top report listing the largest events.
type:         service
kind:         capability
phase:        3
implements:   FEATURE-Top.md
covers:       TOP-001
stack:        python.md, cli.md
provides:     quakes top
consumes:     read_feed, extract_events, filter_events, write_csv, parse_args
depends:      mag-filter, formatting
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  Header time,mag,depth_km,place,id. Sort by mag descending then time ascending, take --n
  (default 10). Filter applies before the cut.

## story daily
summary:      The daily report of events per UTC date.
type:         service
kind:         capability
phase:        3
implements:   FEATURE-Daily.md
covers:       DAY-001
stack:        python.md, cli.md
provides:     quakes daily
consumes:     read_feed, extract_events, filter_events, write_csv, parse_args
depends:      mag-filter, formatting
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  Header date,events,max_mag. One row per date with events, ascending, then TOTAL,<events>,<max>.
  Date is the first 10 characters of the formatted time. No events yields TOTAL,0,.

## story regions
summary:      The regions report of events per region.
type:         service
kind:         capability
phase:        3
implements:   FEATURE-Regions.md
covers:       REG-001
stack:        python.md, cli.md
provides:     quakes regions
consumes:     read_feed, extract_events, filter_events, write_csv, parse_args
depends:      mag-filter, formatting
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  Header region,events,max_mag. Region is the text after the last ", " in place, else the whole
  place; null place is Unknown. Order by events descending then region ascending by byte value.

## story near
summary:      The near report using haversine distance.
type:         service
kind:         capability
phase:        3
implements:   FEATURE-Near.md
covers:       NEAR-001
accepts:      st-004
stack:        python.md, cli.md
provides:     quakes near, haversine_km
consumes:     read_feed, extract_events, filter_events, write_csv, parse_args
depends:      mag-filter, formatting
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  Header distance_km,time,mag,place,id. Haversine on a 6371.0 km sphere. Include events with
  distance <= --radius (compare unrounded distance), ordered by distance ascending then time
  ascending. Distance is written with one decimal, rounded half up.

## story fetch
summary:      The fetch command that downloads a USGS date range to a file.
type:         service
kind:         integration
phase:        3
implements:   FEATURE-Fetch.md
covers:       FETCH-001
accepts:      st-006, st-008
stack:        python.md, cli.md
provides:     quakes fetch, build_url, http_get
consumes:     parse_args, read_feed
depends:      options, exit-codes, feed-validation
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  Request https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query with format=geojson, starttime, endtime,
  minmagnitude (default 2.5), orderby=time-asc, using urllib.request via a single replaceable
  function http_get(url) returning (status, body bytes). Write the body unchanged to --out and print
  fetched,<count>. Tests stub http_get and never open a network connection.

## story fetch-failure
summary:      Fetch fails without writing a file on network, HTTP, or body errors.
type:         service
kind:         capability
phase:        3
implements:   FEATURE-FetchFailure.md
covers:       FETCH-002
stack:        python.md, cli.md
provides:     fetch failure handling
consumes:     http_get
depends:      fetch
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  A network error, status other than 200, or body that is not a FeatureCollection raises
  OperationalError (exit 1) before any file is created. A pre-existing output file is left untouched.

## story test-suite
summary:      Provide bin/test.sh running the pytest suite.
type:         service
kind:         test harness
phase:        2
implements:   FEATURE-TestSuite.md
covers:       TEST-001
accepts:      st-002
stack:        common.md, python.md
provides:     bin/test.sh
depends:      architecture, cli-foundation
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  POSIX sh script that changes to the application root, activates .venv when present, and runs
  pytest -q unfiltered, exiting with pytest's status. Tests stub HTTP and never use the network.

## story verification
summary:      Terminal gate running the supplied grader against the finished application.
type:         feature
kind:         test harness
phase:        4
implements:   VERIFICATION.md
accepts:      st-001, st-003
stack:        common.md
depends:      summary, top, daily, regions, near, fetch-failure, test-suite
acceptance:   yes
instructions: |
  Assembly story. Run sh sources/run.sh with Suite: full and require exit 0, and run sh bin/test.sh
  requiring exit 0. Do not modify anything under sources/.
=== END ARTIFACT ===
=== BEGIN ARTIFACT DECISIONS.json ===
[
  {
    "id": "Q-001",
    "type": "choice",
    "severity": "low",
    "blueprint": "FEATURE-Options.md",
    "story": "options",
    "title": "Usage error exit when an option is repeated",
    "description": "Sources do not say what a repeated option does. Weighed: last wins vs usage error. Chose the narrower, stricter behavior.",
    "options": [
      { "value": "usage-error", "label": "Repeated option is a usage error (exit 2)" },
      { "value": "last-wins", "label": "Last occurrence wins" }
    ],
    "system_choice": "usage-error"
  },
  {
    "id": "Q-002",
    "type": "choice",
    "severity": "low",
    "blueprint": "FEATURE-Formatting.md",
    "story": "formatting",
    "title": "Half-up rounding implementation",
    "description": "Python round() is banker's rounding. Chose decimal.Decimal on the value's repr with ROUND_HALF_UP so 5.125 style values round up as the instructions require.",
    "options": [
      { "value": "decimal-half-up", "label": "Decimal(repr(x)) quantized ROUND_HALF_UP" },
      { "value": "round", "label": "Built-in round()" }
    ],
    "system_choice": "decimal-half-up"
  },
  {
    "id": "Q-003",
    "type": "choice",
    "severity": "low",
    "blueprint": "FEATURE-Fetch.md",
    "story": "fetch",
    "title": "Fetch usage-error and file-write behavior",
    "description": "fetch with missing --start, --end, or --out, or an extra positional argument, is a usage error (exit 2). The output file is written only after the response validates, so failure never creates or alters a file.",
    "options": [

      { "value": "write-then-validate", "label": "Write then remove on failure" }

  }
]
